en.name: iRoomCraft
en.short_description: Interior design from square footage and OCR'd room photos, with local
en.subtitle: Room layout, worked out
en.description:
RoomCraft turns a room's size and purpose into concrete layout advice.

DESIGN
Tell it the room type, the square footage, and the style you are after. RoomCraft returns a design philosophy, a colour palette, a recommended furniture list, and a layout strategy — plus how many pieces the room can actually hold before it stops working.

REDESIGN
Already have notes on what is in the room? Paste them in and RoomCraft works around the fixed elements, giving you a positioning strategy and an ordered set of redesign steps.

SOURCING
Enter coordinates and RoomCraft names the sourcing zone and the material focus that suits it.

HOW IT WORKS
All of it is deterministic rules running on your device — the same inputs always give the same advice, and you can see why. There is no camera, no photo upload, no AI model, and no server. RoomCraft never asks for an account and never sends your room anywhere.

review_information.notes:
Thanks for reviewing iRoomCraft.

A note on the name first: this App Store record is "iRoomCraft" because the original name was already registered to another developer. The app itself, and the home-screen icon, read "Roomcraft", and the in-app header says "RoomCraft".

It is a small offline interior-layout adviser. No account, no sign-in, no demo credentials, no in-app purchase and no network of any kind: every answer is computed on the device by pure functions in lib/domain/ (layout_planner.dart, design_styles.dart, roomcraft_service.dart). It works fully in airplane mode, and the same inputs always produce the same output.

Two things that could read as missing features but are deliberate:
• The Redesign tab carries a document-scanner icon, but there is no camera and no OCR anywhere in the app. You type what is in the room into a text box; the planner looks for the words window, door, fireplace and radiator.
• The Sourcing tab takes a latitude and longitude typed by hand. It never asks for location permission and does not use GPS, and the three suppliers it returns are a fixed built-in example list that is the same for any coordinates - only the zone name changes, above or below latitude 40. It illustrates the idea; it is not a live local directory.

Test instructions:
1. Launch onto the Design tab, pre-filled with "Living Room" and 250 sq ft. Choose a style and tap "Get suggestions" for a design philosophy, a colour palette, a furniture list capped at what the room can hold, and a layout strategy.
2. Change the square footage to 80 and run it again - the number of recommended pieces drops, because the cap is derived from the area.
3. Redesign tab: keep the pre-filled room, type something like "large window on the north wall, radiator under it" into "What is in the room?", pick a target style, then "Plan redesign". You get detected features, positioning advice, a room-size strategy and redesign steps.
4. Sourcing tab: latitude and longitude are pre-filled with 42.3601 / -71.0589. Tap "Find suppliers", then change the latitude to below 40 and run it again to see the zone description change.
5. Entering zero or non-numeric square footage, or an out-of-range coordinate, shows an inline error instead of a result.

Privacy:
• Data collected: nothing. There is no account, no sign-up and no profile, and nothing is written to the device or kept between launches.
• Network: none. The app makes no requests at all.
• Location: none. The coordinates on the Sourcing tab are typed by the user; no location permission is requested and none is declared in Info.plist.
• Tracking: none. There is no advertising or analytics SDK; the advertising identifier is not read and no App Tracking Transparency prompt appears. A Firebase Crashlytics bootstrap is present but inactive - no Firebase configuration file is included.

If you need anything else, please email contact@safecodeg.com and we will respond within one business day.
